historical_growth.growth_rate_source: blend: revenue 10yr CAGR 5.7% (FY2015-FY2025), 3yr 4.8%; the 5yr revenue/EPS figures compound off the COVID-depressed FY2020 base and the 5yr equity CAGR is depressed by the EUR10.1bn Nestlé-stake buyback in FY2021
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 3.8% diverges >30% from revenue 5yr 9.5% and EPS 5yr 12.5%: the FY2021 repurchase of 22.3m shares from Nestlé for EUR8.9bn (FY2021 ShareRepurchases EUR10.06bn) cut book equity from EUR29.0bn to EUR23.6bn. Equity CAGR is not a usable growth proxy for this company; revenue CAGR used instead.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2020 5,331.4 / FY2022 4,696.3 / FY2025 6,745.6. Owner FCF grew slightly slower than reported FCF over 5 years (4.8% vs 5.5%) because interest income rose with the cash pile (EUR19.8m -> 167.7m) and SBC roughly doubled (129.7 -> 248.3); SBC is still only 0.56% of sales so the gap is small. 3yr CAGRs are inflated by the weak FY2022 base (WC outflow, Aesop-era working capital build).

scenario_narratives.base: L'Oréal keeps outperforming a mid-single-digit beauty market by 1-2pp LFL, with ~1pp of that given back to currency on a 66%-ex-eurozone sales base: reported growth 6% in FY2026 (H1 +5.8% reported, Kering Beauté consolidated from April), ~5% through the Gucci-licence years (from July 2027) and decelerating to 3% by year 10. The adjusted EBITDA margin rises ~15-20bp a year to a 25% plateau as Dermatological Beauty and Professional Products outgrow Consumer Products. Tax normalises to 25% after the French surcharge, capex stays 3.5% of sales, leases are an operating cost and the Sanofi and Galderma stakes are carried at market in the bridge. Terminal value at the 20x house cap (Gordon at 7.25%/2.5% would give 21.6x).
scenario_narratives.bull: Full China/Travel Retail recovery, double-digit derm and professional, Luxe re-accelerating on Creed/Kering Beauté/Gucci, emerging markets at 40% of growth: 6.5-7% reported growth for three years, adjusted EBITDA margin to 26.5%, 22x exit.
scenario_narratives.bear: China recovery stalls, strong euro, indie/DTC and Chinese-champion share loss force A&P up: 2.5% reported growth after FY2026, adjusted EBITDA margin back to 23%, 18x exit. A de-rating, not a solvency event.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value L'Oréal as what it is: a very high-quality, slow-compounding consumer franchise whose owner cash flow (after SBC, leases, a recurring restructuring/litigation charge and normalised tax) is ~13.5% of sales and grows mid-single digits. The house model refuses to pay more than 20x owner FCF at exit for the base case and discounts at a EUR-built 7.25%; the Sanofi and Galderma stakes are added at market because their dividends are not in the flows. The result is deliberately well below a market that pays 33x earnings for the same cash flows; the gap between house IV and price is the premium the market attaches to L'Oréal's duration and defensiveness, and the required-return table shows which discount rate the current price implies.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal multiple: the 20x owner-FCF cap binds in the base case; L'Oréal has traded at 25-40x earnings for a decade, so a reader who believes the premium is permanent should look at the bull case (22x) and the required-return table rather than the base IV
China / North Asia and Travel Retail: the highest-margin Luxe division's recovery from the 2023-25 trough is gradual and the single biggest swing between bear and bull
Currency: ~1pp/yr of structural FX drag is assumed in the growth path; a weaker euro would add directly to reported growth and margin
Non-operating stakes (~EUR30/share): Sanofi (EUR6.5bn) and Galderma (EUR9.8bn) are marked at 23 Oct 2026 prices and move with those shares; refresh_price.py does not update them

M&A cadence: 2025-26 outflows (Kering Beauté ~EUR4bn, Galderma EUR2.3bn, Dr.G, Medik8, Color Wow, Innovist) are financed with debt that sits in the bridge while their contribution is only partly in FY0 revenue; further large deals would raise net debt ahead of the flows
Timing: FY0 is calendar 2025 while the balance sheet is 30 June 2026, overstating value by roughly EUR4/share (see inputs.timing_note)

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API regularMarketPrice at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 338.85-438.65; Sanofi (SAN.PA), Galderma (GALD.SW) and EURCHF=X from the same endpoint on the same date for the equity bridge
data_sources.financials: OR.PA_Metrics.csv / core_metrics via make dcf-context (FY2013-FY2025 annuals, H1 FY2013-H1 FY2026); OR.PA_Annual_FY2025.txt (URD 2025: cash flow statement, note 3.2 D&A incl ROU, note 6.2 tax analysis, EPS note); OR.PA_HalfYear_H1-2026.txt (30 June 2026 balance sheet, note 8.1 borrowings and lease debt, note 9.1 investments, note 10.3 share count)
data_sources.qualitative: OR.PA_Analysis.json (2026-10-26): divisions, geographic mix, guidance (no numerical FY2026 target; 'another year of growth in sales and profit'), bull/bear points

inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 532,386,540 shares on issue at 30 June 2026 (H1 2026 report note 10.3) plus ~1.4m dilutive free-share instruments (H1 2026 diluted weighted average 534,722,682 vs basic ~533.4m). Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows; the EUR500m/yr buyback (1.40m shares cancelled in H1 2026) is the cash mechanism that keeps the count flat and is value-neutral here.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 URD cash flow statement, 'share-based payment (including free shares)' EUR248.3m (OR.PA_Annual_FY2025.txt:20162). L'Oréal settles free shares from treasury/new shares with no separate equity-award tax withholding line (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 in kpis), so the combined figure equals the add-back.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 'Disposal/(acquisition) of Treasury shares' EUR501.5m, FY2024 EUR497.5m, H1 2026 EUR501.4m: a steady EUR500m/yr programme, shares cancelled on repurchase. Funded repurchaser.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-23T15:37:31Z regular close (Euronext Paris); valuation written Monday 2026-10-26 before the open
inputs.wacc_rationale: EUR flows discounted at a EUR-built rate: 10y Bund ~2.7% + beta 0.9 x ERP 5.0% = cost of equity ~7.2%; pre-tax cost of debt ~3.0% (Aa1/AA rated, 2025-26 bond issues) = 2.25% after tax; net debt is ~4% of EV so WACC ~7.0%. Rounded up to 7.25% and held IDENTICAL across bear/base/bull: cyclicality (Luxe/Travel Retail/China), FX and competition risk are priced in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked into the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: full lease cash outflow (FY2025 principal EUR453.6m + lease interest EUR58.4m = EUR512.0m, 1.16% of sales; H1 2026 EUR248.4m, 1.04%) charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path at 1.15%. Lease liabilities (EUR2,375.4m at 30 June 2026) are therefore EXCLUDED from net debt, and da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use (FY2025 EUR1,652.4m total less EUR482.5m ROU = EUR1,169.9m, 2.66% of sales) so cash-tax EBIT is not charged twice.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated; NCI stock of EUR48.5m (30 June 2026) deducted once in equity_bridge. NCI profit share is EUR6-8m/yr, immaterial.
inputs.non_operating_assets_note: Matching-asset rule: the component EBITDA is built from operating profit, which sits ABOVE 'Dividends received' (EUR351.9m FY2025, Sanofi) and 'Finance income on cash' (EUR167.7m) in L'Oréal's income statement, so neither income stream is in the projected flows. Their source assets are added in equity_bridge at market value: Sanofi 88,670,657 shares (7.30%) at EUR74.12 (SAN.PA close 2026-10-23) = EUR6,572m less ~3% French participation-exemption tax leakage on the EUR3,547m gain over the EUR3,025.2m cost = EUR6,466m; Galderma 47,579,528 shares (20%, equity-accounted since Feb 2026) at CHF191.05 (GALD.SW 2026-10-23) / EURCHF 0.9237 = EUR9,841m less ~3% leakage on the gain over the EUR8,082m PPA value = EUR9,788m; other non-consolidated investments at carrying value EUR678.6m. The EUR507.2m Galderma-related liability exercisable in 2029 stays inside borrowings. Pension surplus assets (EUR564.6m) and retirement provisions (EUR667.8m) are both left out.
inputs.other_income_expenses_note: L'Oréal's 'Other income and expenses' line (restructuring, impairments, litigation; EUR449.9m / 437.7m / 505.4m in 2023-25, EUR300.5m in H1 2026 incl. EUR169m product-liability costs) recurs every year. ~0.7pp of sales is charged against the adjusted EBITDA margin as the recurring cash portion (impairments excluded), so the FY2025 anchor is 24.5% raw (OP 8,891.9 + D&A 1,652.4 + SBC 248.3 = 10,792.6 / 44,052) less 0.7pp = 23.8%.
inputs.fy0_component_check: FY2025 component build at the anchors (23.8% adj EBITDA, 0.56% SBC, 1.16% lease, 2.66% D&A ex-ROU, 25% normalised cash tax, 3.4% capex, WC neutral) gives owner FCF ~EUR6.0bn (13.6% of sales). Cross-check from the cash flow statement: reported FCF 7,161.6 - SBC 248.3 - interest income 167.7 - Sanofi dividends 351.9 - lease outflow 512.0 - one-off WC inflow 327.4 + FY2025 French exceptional tax surcharge 252.7 = EUR5,807m (13.2%). The 3% gap is the tax-rate normalisation (FY2025 cash taxes paid 2,390 = 28% of PBT incl. surcharge). last_fcf (6,745.6) follows the contract formula reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income; the projection base is the component build, which additionally strips the dividends (asset in the bridge) and the lease outflow (treatment B).
inputs.timing_note: FY0 flows are FY2025 (calendar year) and the balance sheet is 30 June 2026, the latest filed. The H1 2026 owner FCF (~EUR2.6bn) is already inside June cash while the FY2026 projection year counts it again; end-of-year discounting of a year that is ten months elapsed offsets part of this. Net overstatement is of the order of EUR4/share and is accepted rather than hand-adjusted.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (margins still ramping at year 5), scenario-weighted, run through make build-dcf. Routed via the dcf-methods table row 'Operating company, non-US or cyclical: consumer' -> owner-fcf.md + owner-fcf-adaptations.md (currency, leases, NCI, matching-asset rule read and applied). L'Oréal is the world's largest beauty company (FY2025 sales EUR44.05bn, OP margin 20.2%, net cash flow EUR7.2bn): a cash-generative operating company, not a bank/REIT/LIC/holdco, so the default engine is correct. Reporting and quote currency are both EUR (read off the statements, not the suffix). Fresh build, no prior DCF. Terminal value is min(Gordon, cap x FCF_N): at 7.25% WACC the 20x house cap binds in the base case (Gordon would be 21.6x), 22x in bull, 18x in bear. Interest income is stripped from last_fcf because the component flows exclude finance income and cash is netted in the bridge, not because net cash is material (the group is net-debt EUR10.3bn ex leases after Kering Beauté/Galderma).

bear.narrative: FY2026 lands at +5% (H1 already banked) but the China/Travel Retail recovery stalls, a strong euro keeps converting mid-single-digit LFL into ~2.5% reported growth, and share loss in US makeup/mass skincare to indie, DTC and Chinese champions (e.l.f., Rare Beauty, Proya) plus Amazon/Douyin platform leverage forces A&P up ~1pp of sales to defend brands. The adjusted EBITDA margin slips to 23.0% (OP margin ~19.3%, back to 2023 levels); integration of the 2025-26 acquisition wave (Kering Beauté, Dr.G, Medik8, Color Wow, Innovist) delivers less than paid for. Exit at 18x owner FCF, 2% terminal growth. No solvency axis: the bear is a de-rating of a still-profitable franchise.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +6.0% reported: H1 2026 was +5.8% reported (+6.8% LFL) with Kering Beauté consolidated from April and the H1 FX drag (-2.8%) easing to ~-0.6% for the full year per the H1 report. Thereafter LFL ~+5% (beauty market mid-single-digit plus 1-2pp outperformance) less ~1pp structural FX drag on a 66%-ex-eurozone sales base, with the Gucci licence (from July 2027) and Innovist inside the 5% years, decelerating to 3% by year 10.
base.margin_rationale: Adjusted EBITDA (pre-SBC, after a 0.7pp recurring charge for restructuring/litigation) anchored at 23.8% FY2025; FY2026 24.0% matches the +20bp/yr OP-margin cadence of the last three years (19.8 -> 20.0 -> 20.2%, H1 2026 21.3% vs 21.1%), then +15bp/yr to a 25.0% plateau (OP margin ~21.3%) as Dermatological Beauty (26% OP margin) and Professional Products outgrow Consumer Products.
base.tax_rationale: FY2026 27.5% carries the reduced French exceptional surcharge (EUR188m booked in H1 2026) on top of the ~25% structural rate (theoretical 25.1%, -1.9pp rate differences, +1pp permanent differences, +0.2pp Pillar 2); 25% thereafter.
base.capex_wc_rationale: Capex 3.5% of sales (FY2023-25 3.4-3.8%, H1 2026 3.0%) against D&A ex-ROU 2.7% (rising with acquired-intangible amortisation). Working capital modelled on the CHANGE in revenue at -3% capture: receivables + inventories (~EUR10bn) roughly match payables + other current liabilities, so growth consumes a little cash (FY2023 -395, FY2024 -227, FY2025 +327 one-off inflow).

bull.narrative: China/North Asia and Travel Retail complete their recovery (North Asia LFL back to high single digits), Dermatological Beauty and Professional Products hold double-digit LFL, Luxe re-accelerates on Kering Beauté, Creed and the Gucci licence, and emerging markets (SAPMENA-SSA, India via Innovist, Latin America) keep contributing ~40% of growth. Reported growth runs 6.5-7% for three years. Mix (derm 26% OP margin, pro, Luxe fragrance) plus AI-driven A&P efficiency lifts the adjusted EBITDA margin to 26.5% (OP margin ~22.8%). Exit at 22x owner FCF, 3% terminal growth.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 20x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: House default is 15/50/35; moved to 20/50/30. Bear up 5pp because the three bear axes (China/Travel Retail, structural EUR strength, indie and Chinese-champion share loss) are live in the FY2025 numbers (North Asia +0.5% LFL, Luxe flat reported, FY2025 EPS ex non-recurring +0.4%) and the stock sits at the top of its 52-week range. Bull down 5pp because the bull case needs China recovery AND sustained margin expansion at a 20%+ margin AND the 2025-26 acquisition wave to integrate cleanly. No going-concern or covenant axis (Aa1-rated, net debt/EBITDA well under 1x even after Kering Beauté), so the bear is not weighted higher.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
